correctness.rationale: Projective scalar pair counting gives exactly 4n=p^r−1 distinct nonzero syndromes; each local check pair is proportional, making HJH^T zero term-by-term; projective coverage gives rank r. Distinct radius-one syndromes exclude undetectable joint-Lee weight ≤2. Each line has a (1,2) coordinate supporting X_i Z_i² of weight 3 with zero syndrome; columns outside i span, proving it is not a stabilizer. Restricted-class obstruction follows from parity of sign-orbits in every projective line. Exact finite tests at p/r=5/2,5/3,5/4,13/2,17/2 corroborate and do not substitute for proof.

The novelty pertains to symplectically compatible pairing of classical full syndromes and its parity obstruction, not to projective Hamming matrices or the published small parameters. value.rationale: The new Lee-metric framework has only isolated joint-Lee distance-three qudit examples listed at p≥5; an explicit high-rate perfect code for every r≥2 and every p≡1 mod4 fills a motivated infinite-family gap. The congruence obstruction is sharp within the natural coordinatewise-collinear class enforcing termwise symplectic commutativity. The result provides exact constructive syndromes and a proof of distance-three optimality rather than merely rechecking a small table row.
